parsed_profile_json.reason_for_revision: To improve TIL language and clarity.
parsed_profile_json.purpose: To inform 7F.05 users of front end compressor inspections to improve unit availability and reliability.

scope_of_work: During planned borescope inspections (BIs): Inspect 100% of the VSV2s for evidence/signs of tip loss or tip indications.
During planned borescope inspections (BIs): Inspect 100% of the 2-3 T-Fairings for rubs/severe rubs; document the conditions of each T-Fairing so that rubs can be monitored over time.

During planned major inspections or planned outages when the compressor is exposed: Inspect the condition of VSV2 tips and document any rubs or tip curl with photographs; following this, tip the VSV2s to increase the radial clearance (per GE guidance).

During planned major inspections or planned outages when the compressor is exposed: Inspect the 2-3 T-Fairing flow path surface and edges for evidence/signs of high metal, burrs, or rubs; if noted, document with pictures and contact GE for evaluation/disposition.

During planned major inspections or planned outages when the compressor is exposed: Inspect the 2-3 T-Fairing flow path surface and edges for evidence of high metal, burrs, or rubs; document with pictures and contact GE representative for evaluation and disposition by GE engineering.
Provide inspection results to GE representative for evaluation and disposition by GE engineering.

During planned major inspections or planned outages when the compressor is exposed.

parsed_profile_json.hardware_or_part_configuration_text: 7F.05 compressors have a 14 stage compressor starting with rotor stage 1 (R1) and ending with rotor stage 14 (R14). The first three stages of stator vanes on a 7F.05 are variable stator vanes (VSVs). For 7F.05 compressors, there are two stages of T-Fairings: the 1-2 T-Fairing is between the stage 1 and stage 2 compressor blades, and the 2-3 T-Fairing is between the stage 2 and stage 3 compressor blades.

source_snippets.snippet:
During planned borescope inspections, it is recommended to:
1. Inspect 100% of the VSV2s for evidence of tip loss or tip indications.
2. Inspect 100% of the 2-3 T-Fairings for rubs. Document the conditions of each T-Fairing so that rubs can be monitored over time.

During planned major inspections or planned outages when the compressor is exposed, it is recommended to:
1. Inspect the condition of VSV2 tips and document any rubs or tip curl with photographs. Following this, it is recommended to tip the VSV2s to increase the radial clearance.

Inspect the 2-3 T-Fairing flow path surface and edges for evidence of high metal, burrs, or rubs. If high metal, burrs, or rubs are noted, please document the condition of the T-Fairing's with pictures.
This TIL can be deemed complete if the vanes are tipped to increase the clearance or replaced with the VSV2s that have an increased tip clearance.
The above borescope inspections are recurring until the below actions are completed.

The annual inspections of VSV2 and 2-3 TF can be performed during the recommended inspection in TIL 2212.
Therefore, if the inspections in TIL 2212 are performed then annual inspections recommended per TIL 2167 are complete.
During a planned borescope inspection on a 7F.05, tip loss and tip indications were noted on one stage 2 variable stator vane (VSV2). Minor object damaged was noted on downstream compressor airfoils.

For MIs: A qualified and competent GE blade technician. A competent and qualified non-destructive testing (NDT) inspector for post tipping NDT. For this work, NDT is considered a penetrant inspection. Fluorescent penetrant inspection (FPI) is recommended. Red dye penetrant, if FPI is not available, is acceptable NDT as well.
